The trial court held the petitioner guilty and convicted him for various offences including Section 377 IPC wherein the convicted petitioner is sentenced to rigorous imprisonment of 7 years and for offence under Section 376(2)(f) IPC, the convicted petitioner is sentenced to life imprisonment vide judgment dated 29 th January, 2014 and that came to be affirmed on dismissal of the appeal preferred by the review petitioner and later by this Court on dismissal of the special leave petition.
The review petition filed at the instance of the petitioner, in the first instance was rejected by this Court vide Order dated 22 nd REVIEW PETITION (CRIMINAL) NO. 683 OF 2016 November, 2016.

Thereafter, it was urged in the Curative Petition(Criminal) No. 33 of 2021 as follows: Petitioner submits that the order directing the sentence to run one after another has resulted in miscarriage of justice.
Vide order dated 27th September, 2022 in the curative petition, the order dated 22nd November, 2016 dismissing the review petition was recalled.

We have heard learned senior counsel for the review petitioner and are of the view that the sentence which has been awarded to the review petitioner for offence under Section 377 IPC and Section 376(2)
(f) IPC to run consecutively one after the other in terms of Section 31 of the Code of Criminal Anwar Ul-Haque vs State Of Nct on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94800188/
1 Procedure, 1973 and we clarify that the sentence which has been awarded under Section 377 IPC for 7 years rigorous imprisonment has to precede and thereafter the petitioner has to undergo life imprisonment on account of his conviction under Section 376(2)(f) IPC for life in terms of the Constitution Bench Judgment of this Court in Muthuramalingam and Others Vs. State represented by Inspector of Police (2016) 8 SCC 313 wherein in para 35 it has been held as under: The last question is whether the court can direct life REVIEW PETITION (CRIMINAL) NO. 683 OF 2016 sentence and term sentences to run consecutively.

entities.text: Muthuramalingam and Others Vs. State represented by Inspector of Police (2016) 8 SCC 313
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The power of the court to direct the order in which sentences will run is unquestionable in view of the language employed in Section 31 CrPC.
The court can, therefore, legitimately direct that the prisoner shall first undergo the term sentence before the commencement of his life sentence.
Such a direction shall be perfectly legitimate and in tune with Section 31 CrPC.
The converse however may not be true for if the court directs the life sentence to start first it would necessarily imply that the term sentence would run concurrently.
That is because once the prisoner spends his life in jail, there is no question of his undergoing any further reference.

In terms of the view expressed by the Constitution Bench Judgment of this Court in Muthuramalingam and Others(supra) and what has been observed by us, the review petition is without substance and accordingly dismissed.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
